recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. No core FHIR source follow-up is needed for FHIR-12392 unless Pharmacy later decides to change Medication.status semantics again; any future edit should preserve the non-formulary distinction and the FHIR-32482 record-currentness wording.
issue_request: FHIR-12392 was a Published Pharmacy change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification for DSTU2, asking for an active/inactive indication on Medication. The accepted resolution added Medication.status as a 0..1 code with active, inactive, and entered-in-error values, added it as a search parameter, and clarified that the status is not intended to indicate formulary membership.
initial_application: The Jira application comment points to git-svn commit 1854c20643b58916f4f9e00d51f54e942579f38b. Although the commit text appears to typo the tracker as TR#12391, the patch added Medication.status, the MedicationStatus required binding/code list, active/inactive/entered-in-error codes, and a status search parameter to the then-authoritative Medication spreadsheet source. The current XML source carries that application forward through the later source rework.
additional_context: Medication is an active current-build resource and Pharmacy work-group artifact in source/fhir.ini. Current source/medication/structuredefinition-Medication.xml defines Medication.status as 0..1 code, required-bound to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/medication-status, and includes the formulary caveat. source/medication/bundle-Medication-search-params.xml contains the Medication-status token search parameter. source/medication/codesystem-medication-status.xml contains active, inactive, and entered-in-error. Later Published issue FHIR-32482 intentionally changed the value definitions away from the original availability wording to record-currentness wording; its fixed commit is already on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current build source already contains the Medication.status element, required terminology, and search parameter requested by FHIR-12392, and the later FHIR-32482 wording is the current approved interpretation of those status codes.
